title: Antipsychotic adherence and relapse prevention in schizophrenia
bottleneck: Non-adherence drives most schizophrenia relapses, hospitalizations, and functional decline, yet it is treated as a patient compliance problem rather than a systems design problem. Long-acting injectables reduce relapse but are underused due to cost, logistics, and patient and clinician resistance.
why_it_blocks: Relapse in schizophrenia is often preventable, and each psychotic episode may worsen long-term prognosis. The gap between available prevention and actual prevention is one of psychiatry's largest avoidable harms.
current_state: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics are recommended earlier in guidelines but still prescribed late. Digital adherence monitoring and shared decision-making models aim to close the gap with mixed uptake. Long-acting injectables cut relapse roughly in half versus oral drugs in mirror-image studies, yet they remain a last resort in practice rather than the early option guidelines suggest.
